title: Majorana signatures in an asymmetrically coupled quantum dot--topological superconducting nanowire junction
authors: Levente Máthé, Ioan Grosu, Liviu P. Zârbo, Ionel Ţifrea
abstract: We present a theoretical study of the quantum transport through a nanoscale system in which a central quantum dot (QD) is coupled asymmetrically to normal leads and to two Majorana bound states (MBSs) localized at the ends of a topological superconducting nanowire threaded by a tunable magnetic flux. The effects of the leads--QD coupling asymmetry parameter $α$ and the bias voltage asymmetry parameter $q$ on the system's linear conductance are considered for the case of unhybridized and hybridized MBSs. In the zero-temperature limit, for unhybridized MBSs the system's linear conductance is finite only when the magnetic flux phase $φ= (2n+1)π$ ($n\in\mathbb{Z}$) and it scales as $\mathcal{G}=2qαe^2/[h(α+1)]$, while for hybridized MBSs it presents a complicated dependence on the system's parameters. At finite temperature, for unhybridized MBSs, the system's linear conductance oscillates as a function of the magnetic flux phase $φ$ with a period of $2π$, and the position of the linear conductance maxima can be shifted from $φ=2nπ$ to $φ=(2n+1)π$ by simply varying the value of the bias voltage asymmetry parameter $q$. For hybridized MBSs, the conductance exhibits a similar behavior when the energy level of the central QD, $\varepsilon_d$, is tuned at the leads' Fermi level ($\varepsilon_d=\varepsilon_F$), although when $\varepsilon_d\neq\varepsilon_F$ the oscillation period changes to $4π$, and the position of the linear conductance maxima depends on the actual value of $\varepsilon_d$ and other parameters in the system. Our results highlight the experimental importance of the leads-QD and bias voltage asymmetry parameters, which are often present in realistic experimental setups, and can strongly affect the identification and observation of MBSs transport signatures.
summary: This theoretical study models quantum transport through a quantum dot coupled to Majorana bound states in a superconducting nanowire. By analyzing the linear conductance, the authors predict distinct oscillatory behaviors dependent on magnetic flux and bias voltage asymmetries. The findings emphasize that these asymmetry parameters are critical factors that must be accounted for when interpreting experimental measurements of MBS signatures.
main_problem: The study investigates the quantum transport signatures of Majorana Bound States (MBSs) through a quantum dot coupled asymmetrically to a topological superconducting nanowire junction.
main_result: The linear conductance exhibits characteristic oscillations dependent on the magnetic flux phase ($\phi$) and the bias voltage asymmetry parameter ($q$), with periodicity changing based on whether the central QD energy level is tuned to the Fermi level.
method: The analysis employs non-equilibrium Green's function techniques to calculate the linear conductance ($G$) in the subgap regime.
model_or_system: The system consists of a central quantum dot (QD) coupled asymmetrically to normal leads and to two MBSs localized at the ends of a topological superconducting nanowire threaded by a tunable magnetic flux. The Hamiltonian includes terms for leads, MBSs, the QD, and tunneling.
key_observables: Linear conductance ($G$), which is analyzed by decomposing it into electron tunneling ($G_{	ext{ET}}$), local Andreev reflection ($G_{	ext{LAR}}$), and crossed Andreev reflection ($G_{	ext{CAR}}$).
important_parameters: Leads–QD coupling asymmetry ($\alpha$), bias voltage asymmetry ($q$), magnetic flux phase ($\phi$), and the QD energy level ($\epsilon_d$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed in the zero-temperature and finite-temperature limits, assuming the low-energy transport regime.
figures_summary: Figures schematically represent the junction setup and illustrate the dependence of conductance on parameters like $\phi$, $T$, $\alpha$, and $q$.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework using Green's functions, analyzes the conductance components ($G_{	ext{ET}}, G_{	ext{LAR}}, G_{	ext{CAR}}$) separately, and presents results for both unhybridized and hybridized MBSs in both zero and finite temperature regimes.
why_interesting: The explicit dependence of transport signatures on asymmetry parameters ($\alpha, q$) provides crucial, testable predictions for experimental realization and characterization of topological qubits.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic representation of a QD attached to two MBSs hosted by a topological superconducting nanowire loop, threaded by a magnetic flux Φ. The central QD is coupled to two metallic leads (left L and right R) with coupling strengths ΓL and ΓR, respectively. The central QD is also coupled to the two MBSs (denoted by the operators η1 and η2) located at the ends of a topological superconducting nanowire with coupling parameters λ1 and λ2, respectively. The central QD characteristic energy level can be tuned by a gate voltage applied to the gate electrode.

FIG. 2. The zero–temperature linear conductance G (black line) and its components related to electron tunneling GET (red line), local Andreev reflection GLAR (blue line), and crossed Andreev reflection GCAR (green line) as a function of the coupling asymmetry parameter α = ΓL/ΓR in the case of unhybridized MBSs (εM/Γ = 0). The magnetic flux phase is set at ϕ = π. The applied bias voltage asymmetry parameter is (a) q = 0.25, (b) q = 0.5, and (c) q = 0.75.

FIG. 3. The linear conductance G in the case of unhybridized MBSs (εM/Γ = 0) as a function of QD-MBS coupling strength |λ2|/Γ and temperature kBT/Γ for a symmetric leads–QD coupling parameter (α = 1) at different values of the QD–MBS coupling strength |λ1| and bias voltage asymmetry parameter q. The QD characteristic energy level εd/Γ = 0, and the magnetic flux phase ϕ = π. The values of the QD-MBS coupling strength |λ1| are: (a)-(c) |λ1|/Γ = 0.3 and (d)-(f) |λ1|/Γ = 1.2. The bias voltage asymmetry parameter is set to q = 0.25 for (a) and (d), q = 0.5 for (b) and (e), and q = 1 for (c) and (f).

FIG. 4. Total linear conductance G for the case of unhybridized MBSs (εM/Γ = 0) as a function of the coupling asymmetry parameter α at different temperature values (kBT/Γ = 0 – black line, kBT/Γ = 0.3 – red line, and kBT/Γ = 1.2 – blue line) and QD-MBS coupling strengths: (a)-(c) |λ1|/Γ = 0.3, |λ2|/Γ = 0.1 and (d)-(f) |λ1|/Γ = 1.2, |λ2|/Γ = 1. The bias voltage asymmetry parameter q = 0.25 for (a) and (d), q = 0.5 for (b), (e), and q = 1 for (c) and (f). The magnetic flux phase is ϕ = π, and the QD characteristic energy level εd/Γ = 0 (solid lines) and εd/Γ = −1 (dashed lines).

FIG. 5. The total linear conductance G in the case of unhybridized MBSs (εM/Γ = 0) as a function of temperature kBT/Γ at different values of the leads–QD coupling asymmetry parameter (α = 0.5 – black line, α = 1 – red line, and α = 10 – blue line) and different values of the bias voltage asymmetry parameter (a) q = 0.25, (b) q = 0.5 and (c) q = 1. The QD-MBSs coupling strengths are |λ1|/Γ = 0.3 and |λ2|/Γ = 0.1, and the magnetic flux phase is ϕ = π. The solid and dashed lines correspond to the QD characteristic energy level εd/Γ = 0 and εd/Γ = −1, respectively.
